title_en: The Pillars of Islam, Part One
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، أما بعد فإن الله عز وجل سمى هذا الدين الذي أرسل به الرسول الكريم صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الناس كافة دين الإسلام، وختم به الديانات السابقة، وجعله الدين الحق عند الله سبحانه وتعالى، فكل ما سواه من الأديان بعد نزوله وبعثة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم به مردود على أصحابه، لا يتقبل الله منه شيئا، وإن الله عز وجل لم يرض للبرية إلا هذا الدين، وإنما جعل الأديان السابقة له إعدادا له فقط،
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful.

... and I ask God to bless and grant peace to the one who was sent as a mercy to all the worlds, and to his family, his Companions, and all who follow his guidance and keep to his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: God, Mighty and Majestic, named this religion — the religion with which He sent the noble Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to all people — the religion of Islam. With it He sealed the religions that came before, and He made it the true religion in the sight of God, glorified and exalted. So every religion other than it, after its coming down and after the sending of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with it, is thrown back upon those who hold to it: God accepts nothing of it. God, Mighty and Majestic, was content for His creation with no religion but this one, and He made the earlier religions nothing but a preparation for it,
translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

The Arabic opens 'In the name of God...' and then continues with a connective وأصلي ('and I ask God to bless...'), which presupposes a preceding clause. The parallel openings in articles 498, 499 and 516 have الحمد لله رب العالمين ('All praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds') at that point, so a phrase appears to have dropped out of this page. The ellipsis in the English marks the gap; nothing has been supplied.
الديانات السابقة is rendered 'the religions that came before'. The Sheikh gives no further specification of which religions he means, and none has been added.
